spans.s: muṭaka, mūṭaka (IE 8-5; EI 25), a measure or head-load; cf. caṇā-satka-mūṭaka, ‘one mūṭaka of peas’ (LP). See Ep. Ind., Vol. XV, p. 303, text line 50; cf. moṭ (a load) in Hindī and other dialects.
mūṭaka (LP), same as mūḍā, a measure of capacity equal to a hundred or twentyfour maunds; a bullock's load (Ep. Ind., Vol. XIV, p. 309; cf. Marāṭhī mūṭh, ‘a bullock's pack-saddle’).
mu-ṭī, abbreviation of an expression probably meaning ‘a mound covered with jungle’ (Ep. Ind., Vol. XXX, p. 56).
